title: Exploring the Interplay of Life Attitude and Cognitive Ability in Shaping the Intention to Stock Market Participation Among Young Professionals in the Philippines
tldr: Examines how life attitude (purpose, meaning, goal orientation) and cognitive ability (financial literacy) jointly shape stock market participation intentions among 195 young Filipino professionals using PLS-SEM mediation analysis.
problem_and_motivation: The stock market participation puzzle persists despite extensive research on economic, demographic, and cognitive determinants. Broader psychological orientations like life attitude remain underexplored in investment contexts, especially regarding how they interact with cognitive ability. Young professionals in the Philippines, a rapidly growing investor segment, have been neglected despite their unique digital-enabled financial ecosystem.
approach: Quantitative cross-sectional design with 195 young Filipino professionals (aged 20-39) from Bulacan province via simple random sampling.
Survey using Life Attitude Profile-Revised (LAP-R, 7 dimensions) and Financial Literacy Inventory (van Rooij et al., 2011) as cognitive ability proxy.
PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.0 with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) to test direct and mediating effects.
Multi-group analysis across sex (male/female) and education (bachelor's/postgraduate) for cross-group stability.
Harman's single-factor test and full collinearity VIF assessment to rule out common method variance.
Robustness checks with demographic controls (sex, age, education, employment status) and sensitivity analyses.
findings: LAP positively predicts SMP (β = 0.154, p = 0.025); Cognitive Ability mediates LAP→SMP (β = 0.051, p = 0.032).
num: Death Acceptance (DA) strongly predicts SMP (β = 0.312, p < 0.001); Goal Seeking (GS) also significant (β = 0.396, p = 0.009).
num: Life Purpose (LP) shows a negative relationship with SMP (β = −0.243, p = 0.036), suggesting purpose-driven conservatism.
num: Cognitive Ability (C) robustly predicts SMP (β = 0.329, p < 0.001); LAP predicts C (β = 0.158, p = 0.023).
num: Model explains 47.1% of SMP variance (R² = 0.471); with controls, R² increases to 0.496.
num: Sex moderates: males rely more on cognitive ability (β = 0.42); females on life attitude (β = 0.38).
num: Postgraduates show stronger path coefficients than bachelor's holders (C→SMP: β = 0.45 vs. 0.37).
Harman's single-factor test shows first factor explains only 29.32% (< 50% threshold), no CMV concern.
All HTMT values below 0.85 threshold, confirming discriminant validity among LAP constructs.
Fit indices: χ²/df = 1.97, CFI = 0.962, TLI = 0.954, RMSEA = 0.042, SRMR = 0.038.

definitions.definition: Seven-dimension framework measuring life purpose, existential vacuum, life control, death acceptance, will to meaning, goal seeking, and future meaning to fulfill (Reker et al., 1987).
Measured via the Financial Literacy Inventory (van Rooij et al., 2011) covering basic numeracy, inflation comprehension, risk diversification, and investment principles.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Integrates existential psychology (life attitude) with behavioral finance to demonstrate that investment intentions are shaped by sense of meaning, purpose, and cognitive preparedness, not purely rational calculation.
directly_justifies: Odin's user profiling feature can incorporate psychological orientation (life attitude) alongside financial literacy to personalize budgeting recommendations.
Supports the need for financial education modules in Odin that go beyond numeracy to include purpose-driven goal setting.
limits: Limited to Filipino young professionals in Bulacan; may not generalize to other Philippine regions or countries.
Cross-sectional design restricts causal interpretation; longitudinal studies needed.
Self-reported data may introduce social desirability bias.
LAP-R used without local cultural adaptation or pilot testing for the Philippine population.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Study is non-algorithmic and Philippine-origin (local). Focus on behavioral finance, financial literacy, investment behavior, and financial decision-making maps to topics 1.A, 1.C, 4.A, 4.B, 7.B.

limitations: Self-reported survey data may contain response biases and social desirability effects.
Cross-sectional design captures relationships at a single point; causal direction cannot be established.
Sample limited to young professionals in Bulacan province, restricting geographic and demographic generalizability.
No cultural adaptation or pilot testing of LAP-R instrument for the Filipino population.
Financial literacy as proxy may not capture the full breadth of cognitive ability (e.g., abstract reasoning).
Absence of a marker variable for formal CMV testing, though procedural remedies were applied.
remember_this: Life attitude shapes investment intent, mediated by cognitive ability.
Death acceptance and goal seeking increase stock market participation.
Life purpose negatively predicts investment — purpose-driven conservatism.
Men rely on cognition; women on life attitude for investing.
Model explains 47% of SMP variance — strong for behavioral research.
